chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Shurayḥ, who said:

ʿUdhāfir asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, while I was with him, about the leftover water of the cat, sheep, cow, camel, donkey, horse, mule, and beasts of prey: may one drink from it or perform wudu (ablution) from it? He said: “Yes, drink from it and perform wudu (ablution).” He said: I said to him, “The dog?” He said: “No.” I said: “Is it not a beast of prey?” He said: “No, by Allah, it is najis (ritually impure); no, by Allah, it is najis (ritually impure).”

key_terms.سُؤْرِ: leftover water or drink remaining after an animal has drunk from it

ai.seo_question: Can one drink from or perform wudu (ablution) with water left over by animals such as cats, livestock, beasts of prey, and dogs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the leftover water from various animals and its use for drinking and wudu (ablution). It permits the leftover water of several animals, including beasts of prey, while explicitly excluding the dog and affirming its najasah (ritual impurity).
